prompt.context: Our client is a large national health care payer (health insurance company, think Aetna) exploring the launch of a new disease management (DM) program to better serve its 5 million members. The idea is to hire and train a team of Health Coaches to specialize in a single disease area (e.g., heart disease, diabetes, etc.). Each Coach will manage a portfolio of patients to reduce the costs of overall health expenditures (e.g., reminders to take drugs, provide limited medical advice, suggested diet, etc.). Studies show that once-a-month contact with each patient reduces health spending by 5%, on average.
prompt.question: Should our client launch the program? If so, what steps should it take?

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive landscape for disease management programs?
clarifying_info.a: With spiraling health care costs, the industry is under pressure to innovate. Assume the client is first to market. Past attempts to purely automate DM have yielded minimal savings.

clarifying_info.q: How do the Health Coaches operate?
clarifying_info.a: All activity is conducted remotely via phone/email. Typical profile is a registered nurse who wants to work from home. It is difficult to actually reach patients, so Coaches can contact 8 members per day (assume 25 days per month).

clarifying_info.q: What does a Health Coach cost?
clarifying_info.a: Annual cost per Coach: $60K salary + 20% other (training, benefits, laptop, etc.). There are no other program costs.

exhibits.title: Client's member segmentation by health condition
exhibits.shows: A chart breaking down the client's 5 million members across three segments (Group, Individual, and 65+) and showing the prevalence of various health conditions (including diabetes) within each segment as percentages.
exhibits.data: Three segments: Group, Individual, 65+. 65+ segment = 20% of total members. Within 65+ segment, diabetics = 40%. Members 65+ are known as Medicare Advantage, premiums funded by government.

exhibits.title: Average cost data (Per Member Per Month)
exhibits.shows: A table of average Per Member Per Month (PMPM) medical costs by segment, plus a multiplier showing how much more expensive diabetic members are relative to the segment average.
exhibits.data: Individual: avg PMPM $150; Group: avg PMPM $100; 65+: avg PMPM $300. Diabetic factor: 4x the average PMPM for all segments.

framework: Program Savings: identify the right customer segment and disease area to maximize the 5% cost reduction impact; quantify savings per coach
Program Costs: calculate total annual cost per coach (salary + other); determine coach portfolio capacity (members per coach)
Break-even / Profitability: compare per-coach savings vs. per-coach costs; scale to full addressable population
Risks: validate assumptions (5% savings, capacity); competitive response; regulatory and liability considerations

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, which member segment and disease area should the client prioritize for the DM program, and why?
questions.guidance: Strong answer: 65+ (Medicare) patients are the sickest and drive the highest costs, making them the best candidates since the 5% savings will have the largest absolute impact. Within 65+, diabetes is the largest chronic disease category and, as a condition primarily driven by behavior (Type 2), is most responsive to coaching. Individual segment is next most costly; Group members are youngest and healthiest.

questions.prompt: How many 65+ diabetic members does the client have?
questions.guidance: Apply segment percentage and diabetic prevalence rate to the total member base.

math.setup: Total members × 65+ segment share × diabetic prevalence within 65+

questions.prompt: What is the maximum patient portfolio size for one Health Coach?
questions.guidance: Coach can contact 8 members per day and must contact each patient once per month (25 working days). Portfolio = daily capacity × working days per month.

math.setup: Contacts per day × working days per month = maximum patients per coach
steps: 8 contacts/day × 25 days/month = 200 patients per coach per month

questions.prompt: What is the annual cost per Health Coach?
questions.guidance: Base salary plus 20% for training, benefits, and equipment.

questions.prompt: Using both exhibits, calculate the annual savings generated by one Health Coach managing a full portfolio of 65+ diabetics.
questions.guidance: Compute monthly cost per 65+ diabetic patient using the PMPM base and diabetic multiplier, apply the 5% savings rate, then annualize over the full 200-patient portfolio.

math.setup: (Avg PMPM for segment × diabetic factor × 5% savings) × 12 months × portfolio size
steps: 65+ avg PMPM = $300; diabetic factor = 4x → diabetic PMPM = $300 × 4 = $1,200
math.answer: $144,000 in annual savings per Health Coach

questions.prompt: Is the Health Coaching program profitable for the 65+ diabetic segment? What about Individual and Group diabetics?
questions.guidance: Compare per-coach savings to per-coach cost. Then repeat the logic for Individual ($150 PMPM) and Group ($100 PMPM) to show the relative economics.

math.setup: Profit per coach = annual savings per coach − annual cost per coach
steps: 65+ diabetics: $144,000 savings − $72,000 cost = $72,000 profit per coach (2x return)
Individual diabetics: PMPM = $150 × 4 = $600 diabetic; savings = $600 × 5% × 12 × 200 = $72,000; profit = $72,000 − $72,000 = $0 (break-even)
math.answer: 65+ segment: $72,000 profit per coach. Individual segment: break-even. Group segment: $24,000 loss per coach.

questions.prompt: What is the total program profit per year if the client deploys coaches across the entire 65+ diabetic population?
questions.guidance: Divide total addressable 65+ diabetics by portfolio size to get number of coaches needed, then multiply profit per coach.

math.setup: (Total 65+ diabetics ÷ portfolio size) × profit per coach

brainstorming.prompt: There are 650K Group diabetics left uncoached and the segment is currently unprofitable. How might the client make the Group segment work?

categories.name: Increase program efficiency
ideas: Coaching at the workplace to improve reachability
Bi-monthly instead of monthly contact to double portfolio size
Automated correspondence (email, SMS reminders) to supplement coaches
Group coaching sessions to serve multiple patients per contact

categories.name: Generate additional revenue
ideas: Charge employers a fee for the disease management service
Seek government subsidies or grants for preventive care programs
Bundle DM program with group insurance pricing as a value-add

categories.name: Target higher-responding patients
ideas: Since 5% is an average, focus on Group members with highest cost or poorest health metrics who are likely to exceed 5% savings
Use predictive analytics to identify highest-risk/highest-cost Group members

categories.name: Reduce coach cost
ideas: Use lower-cost support staff for routine reminders, reserving registered nurses for complex cases
Offshore or outsource portions of coaching

recommendation: Client should launch the Health Coaching program, focusing first on diabetes in the 65+ Medicare segment
The 65+ diabetic segment generates $72,000 profit per coach per year (a 2x return) and $144 million in total annual profit across 2,000 coaches
Consider extending to the Individual diabetic segment despite break-even economics, for customer retention and ethical reasons
risks: The 5% average savings assumption may not hold in practice; needs validation via a pilot
Coach capacity of 200 patients assumes 8 reachable contacts per day, which may be optimistic
Adding more diabetic members (if marketing externally) will increase overall health care costs even after the 5% reduction
Regulatory and liability risks from nurses providing remote medical advice
next_steps: Launch a controlled pilot program to validate key assumptions: 5% cost reduction, coach portfolio capacity, and patient reachability
Expand to the full 65+ diabetic population after pilot confirms economics
Evaluate Individual diabetic segment for inclusion despite break-even (retention and moral rationale)
Explore options to make Group diabetic segment profitable (employer fees, more efficient delivery model)
Assess opportunity to sell Health Coach services to other payers, including pricing model and regulatory hurdles
